summary: Extends the STIR and SIP error handling for Identity header failures. It lets the Reason header field carry an error back to the authentication service when local policy lets the call proceed despite a verification failure.

plainLanguage.summary: If a caller ID check fails but the call goes through anyway, this sends a note back to say what went wrong.

questions: how to report stir verification failure
sip reason header with identity errors
what is the stir reason header
what is the ppi parameter in sip
how are stir verification errors reported
subtitle: How STIR verification errors travel back to the signing side through the SIP Reason header when a call goes ahead anyway.

tldr.problem: When a STIR Identity check fails, the usual 4xx response ends the call, but some policies want the call to continue and still need the signing side told about the error, even with several Identity headers on one call.
tldr.mechanism: A new Reason header protocol value, STIR, carries the error cause and text in a provisional or final response. A ppi parameter holding the PASSporT, preferably in compact form, says which Identity header failed.
tldr.outcome: The authentication service learns of the error and can fix it, and it MUST remove the Reason header field before the response goes further upstream. The RFC is a Proposed Standard.

today: RFC 9410 is a Proposed Standard published in July 2023. It has not been obsoleted or updated.

sections.title: The Problem with Ending the Call
sections.content:
STIR lets a telephone number or URI-based identity be asserted with a digital signature. In SIP, an authentication service creates a PASSporT and delivers it in an Identity header field. A verification service checks it. The framework is described in RFC 7340 and its SIP use in RFC 8224.

RFC 8224 maps verification failures to 4xx responses, which end the call. In some deployments, policy says calls should continue even when verification fails, for instance after an inadvertent or operational error that is not an attempt at falsification. The authentication service should still hear about the error so that corrective action can be taken.

The document also addresses calls that carry several Identity header fields, where some verify and others do not.
sections.plainLanguage: Sometimes a guard lets someone in even though their badge scan failed. The badge office still needs to know the scan failed so it can fix the problem.

sections.title: Reporting the Error Without Ending the Call
sections.content:
The document defines a new Reason header field protocol value, STIR. Any provisional or final SIP response except 100 (Trying) MAY contain one or more Reason header fields with a STIR-related cause code from RFC 8224 or future specifications.

When local policy says the call should continue despite a verification error, the verification service MUST NOT send the 4xx as a response. Instead it includes the error code and reason phrase in a Reason header field in the next provisional or final response to the authentication service.

Example: Reason: STIR ;cause=436 ;text="Bad Identity Info"
sections.plainLanguage: Instead of slamming the door, the checker lets the call through and quietly slips a note into the next reply saying what went wrong.

sections.title: Pointing at the Right Identity Header
sections.content:
When a message has several Identity header fields and one has an error, the verification service MUST report the error in a Reason header field in the next provisional or final response. For a SIP INVITE with multiple Identity headers, a ppi parameter on the Reason header is RECOMMENDED. It names the failing Identity header by including its PASSporT.

The PASSporT can appear in full form or in compact form, where only the signature is included with two periods as a prefix. Compact form is recommended because full form may include information with privacy or security implications.

If several Identity headers fail, the verification service MUST include one Reason header field per error, each with cause, text and normally ppi. Sending several Reason headers with the same protocol value relies on the update in RFC 9366.
sections.plainLanguage: If a bag of tickets has a bad one, the note quotes the end of the bad ticket so the printer knows exactly which one to look at, without copying the whole ticket.

sections.title: Removal and Security
sections.content:
When the authentication service receives a Reason header field carrying a PASSporT it generated, it should first follow local policy, for example logging or alarming. Then it MUST remove that Reason header field, so the PASSporT does not travel upstream to a User Agent Client or Server that may not be authorized to see its claims.

The security section explains why. In some call flows, such as diversion-based ones, the signer may not be the first-hop initiator, so passing PASSporT data further could raise privacy or security concerns, including replay of a potentially still-fresh PASSporT. Compact form is RECOMMENDED to limit exposure.
sections.plainLanguage: The note quotes part of a ticket, so the ticket printer must tear it up after reading it. That way nobody else can see or reuse what was on it.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content: IANA registered two items. In the "Reason Protocols" registry it added protocol value STIR with protocol cause "STIR Error code", referencing RFC 8224. In the "Header Field Parameters and Parameter Values" registry it added the Reason header field parameter ppi, with no predefined values, referencing RFC 9410.
sections.plainLanguage: The two new words, STIR and ppi, were added to the official list of names so nobody uses them for something else.
